subject: Data retention exception request - FinServe

Subject: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's call - data retention/PII

Hi Elena — great to meet you and the FinServe team this morning. Thanks for walking us through the use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of FinServe requirements (as I heard them):
- No retention of PII/request bodies (0-retention) for production traffic if possible
- Audit logs limited/shortened (requested 30 days or less)
- Data residency: US-East for all production workloads
- Encryption at-rest/in-transit, SOC 2 evidence and DPA language required

Open questions for us to validate:
1) Is 0-retention feasible on Redwood's hosted API or would this require Dedicated/Private deployment?
2) If we can't do full 0-retention, can we offer a shortened logs option (e.g., strip request bodies, retain hashed IDs only) and what are the operational tradeoffs?
3) Any procurement/legal timeline we should be aware of?

Proposed next steps:
- I'll loop in Camila and Rafael to provide technical feasibility and a short spec for ephemeral/short-retention options (Camila: can you share the spec + tradeoffs?)
- Elena: if you can share the security questionnaire / sample contract language we can align on the DPA redlines (you mentioned procurement was involved)
- Quick alignment call early next week with security/procurement if that helps (we're flexible)

Attachments: Data_Retention_SLA_v1.pdf (high level options)

Thanks — Marissa

--

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's call - data retention/PII

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple clarifications from my side (security and procurement are cc'd):

- Our security requirement is strict: no storage, indexing, or logging of full request payloads containing PII. We typically ask vendors for a contractual 0-retention exception for PII. Small audit logs are ok but need to be scrubbed of PII and retained no longer than 30 days.
- Procurement: timeline is ~4-6 weeks to finalize vendor paperwork once security signs off. We will need a DPA and the typical infosec questionnaire answered. I've attached the security questionnaire for your team to review (FinServe_Security_Questionnaire.pdf).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can either: 1) run in a mode that never persists request bodies for production traffic; or 2) provide a dedicated/private deployment where logs can be controlled and data residency guaranteed? If neither is available, we will need clear contract language that guarantees immediate deletion on request and limited logging.

Elena
Director, Product Security
FinServe Capital

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's call - data retention/PII

Hi Elena — thanks for the questionnaire, and good questions. High-level technical options from Redwood's side and the tradeoffs: 

Option A — Ephemeral / 0-retention mode (recommended for PII-sensitive workloads):
- Behavior: request bodies and generated outputs are not written to persistent logs. KV cache kept strictly in-memory and evicted; no persistent request logs.
- Requirements: Only available on Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private deployments today for production-grade SLAs. We can run a managed ephemeral mode in hosted for trial under strict contract, but that requires legal/ops sign-off.
- Tradeoffs: no request-level observability (limiting debugging), limited access to token-level billing metrics, reduced anomaly-detection capabilities.

Option B — Shortened logs / redaction (typical hosted compromise):
- Behavior: we strip full request bodies from logs, persist hashed request IDs and high-level metadata, retain audit logs for configurable window (e.g., 7/30 days).
- Requirements: Works on hosted API with DPA + contractual commitments.
- Tradeoffs: Some telemetry available for support; still meets most security/compliance controls if configured correctly.

Operational notes:
- Data residency can be guaranteed by routing to US-East regions and pinning accounts to that region.
- SOC 2 evidence and DPIA materials are available; we can share SOC 2 Type II report under NDA.

I've attached a short spec that outlines the ephemeral option and the exact flags/config we recommend (ephemeral_mode_spec.pdf). Rafael — can you help draft the proposed contract language that covers the 0-retention exception + DPA redlines?

Next suggested step: 30-min technical call with FinServe Security and our security/compliance (Monica) so we can triage feasibility and surface any operational constraints. Marissa — want me to propose times?

Thanks,
Camila

--

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-04-16T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Proposed contract language for 0-retention / shortened logs

Team — looping in Monica for legal/compliance review. Draft language below (first pass):

"Vendor agrees to implement and maintain, for the duration of the Agreement, a data handling configuration under which (i) request payloads containing PII will not be persistently stored or indexed (\"Ephemeral Mode\"), and (ii) audit metadata may be retained for a maximum of thirty (30) calendar days solely for operational diagnostics and security monitoring. Vendor will route all production workloads for Customer to the US-East region and encrypt data at rest and in transit. The parties agree to execute a mutually acceptable Data Processing Addendum (DPA) that incorporates this configuration."

Notes:
- The Ephemeral Mode clause is feasible for Dedicated/Private; for hosted engagements we can offer Ephemeral Mode with additional contractual commitments and an operational review.
- We should be explicit about debug/support workflows (e.g., joint debugging sessions rather than snapshotting logs).

Monica — please advise on whether the above is acceptable or if legal needs stricter wording. Also flag anything we should not commit to on hosted by default.

Rafael
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@finserve.com>
Date: 2026-04-16T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Proposed contract language for 0-retention / shortened logs

Thanks Rafael — reviewed the draft. High-level guidance:

- We can sign off on the proposed Ephemeral Mode language for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- For hosted API we should not commit to full 0-retention by default. Instead offer a contractual exception that is supported only if Customer: (a) signs the DPA with the redlines; and (b) agrees to a security operations playbook (joint debugging; no snapshots).

- Suggested change: shorten audit metadata retention to 7 days where possible. 30 days is doable but customer-preferred 7-day window is reasonable as a negotiation point.

Suggested contractual wording (final):
"Vendor will implement Ephemeral Mode for Customer's production workloads, such that request payloads containing PII are not persistently stored or indexed. Audit metadata will be retained for a maximum of seven (7) calendar days unless otherwise agreed by the parties in writing. For hosted deployments, Ephemeral Mode will be provided subject to execution of the parties' DPA and an operational security playbook governing debugging and support."

Attachments: DPA_redlines.docx

Marissa — recommend proposing two options to FinServe in writing: (1) Dedicated/Private + Ephemeral Mode + 7-day audit retention (strongest guarantee), and (2) Hosted + redaction/shortened logs + 7/30-day retention with explicit operational constraints. Ask them to confirm preferred route and whether procurement/legal want to see our DPA redlines now.

Monica Patel
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
Notes: thread next steps: schedule 30-min call w/ FinServe security + procurement; Marissa to propose times; attach DPA redlines and ephemeral spec; Rafael to prepare legal-friendly clause for procurement; Camila to prepare short technical spec for ephemeral mode and operational limitations.
